title: Harmon toolchain floors
description: The toolchain floors a harmon-init release declares: the oldest version of each tool that release's template output works with. Each release tag's copy is that release's declaration; consumers read it from the frozen template commit and never render it. scripts/validate-toolchain-floors.sh (task validate:toolchain-floors) keeps the template's own pins at or above every floor.

floor.description: One tool's floor. `compare` selects how a pin's captured value is held to `minimum`: major = integer major at least the minimum; version = dotted numeric at least the minimum; ancestor = the pinned harmon-init commit descends from the minimum commit (how an image digest gets a floor at all, since its tag names the commit it was built from). `when` names a boolean Copier answer gating the floor; absent, the floor always applies. A gate is evaluated against the target template's resolved answers, computed ones such as use_node included, which are never saved in .copier-answers.yml (how a consumer obtains them is the standardize-repo skill's concern). `pins` may be empty for a tool whose only template-side declaration lives in copier.yml (copier: checked against _min_copier_version).

pin.description: Where a floor's tool is pinned. `path` is the location in a generated repository. `template_path` is the literal template source path, including any Jinja in the filename, or null for a repository-owned pin. `pattern` is a JavaScript regular expression with the pinned value or comparison component in capture group 1. By default it applies to whole file text with the multiline flag: rendered YAML for step pins, raw template text for other template pins, and the consumer's own file text for consumer validation. If `json_pointer` is set, it applies to the string at that pointer instead. A step with `pattern_scope: value` applies it to the parsed scalar of its selected input. A missing literal template source is an error. A step pin must render in at least one checked profile.

step.description: Select direct action steps in rendered workflow or composite-action YAML and require exactly one recognized input in each. With the default whole-file scope, capture group 1 must start at the parsed input's value position, and all whole-file matches are checked, including outside covered steps. With value scope, all matches are checked within the parsed input of each selected step. The parsed value must equal the capture, with dotted numeric components allowed after a major capture. Flow-style mappings are unsupported.
